claim: Skype for Windows 8 Metro app: full-screen Metro/Modern redesign, live tile for missed calls/messages, Snap mode, Windows Store distribution.
Desktop Skype 6.0 for Windows/Mac released October 2012, distinct from Windows 8 Metro app.
Group video calling became free for all users April 28, 2014, rolling out to Windows/Mac/Xbox One, up to 10 people.
Group video calling had been a premium/paid service since exiting beta (~early 2011) until April 2014.
As of Sept 16, 2014 minimum Windows requirement was Vista, cutting out XP; Mac minimum became OS X 10.5 Leopard with Core 2 Duo.
Mac OS X 10.4 Tiger support dropped in same 2014 change.
Last Skype version usable on Windows XP was 7.36.0.150.
Skype 6.0.0.120 for Windows released Oct 24, 2012, with Windows 8 Metro companion.
Skype 6.0 UI 'flattened,' Don't-call-it-Metro-friendly UI on Windows.
Skype 6.0 added sign-in with Facebook or Microsoft account; Live Messenger/Hotmail/Outlook.com accounts qualified.
After merging Microsoft Account with Skype Account, users got all Messenger contacts plus existing Skype contacts.
Tools > Options > Advanced had a 'Help improve Skype...' telemetry checkbox.
Metro app app-bar (swipe down / right-click) revealed add-contact/save-number options.
Modern app settings reached via Charms bar (swipe from right / hover bottom-right), not Tools>Options.
Modern app home screen showed active IM conversations across the top, tappable to resume.
Modern app conversation view full-screen with back arrow; file sharing via plus-button 'send files'.
Modern app call window: profile + camera/voice/IM/file buttons; dial pad lacked backspace key.
Modern app lacked call recording and other desktop-only tools.
Desktop sharing in Modern app only worked PC-to-Modern, not reverse.
72 standard Skype emoticons in program (5.5-6.14 era).
Skype 6.14 added hidden emoticons (talktothehand, dog, shielddeflect, idea, sheep, blackwidow, bike, nickfury, bucky, cat, captain).
Hidden emoticons (finger), (fubar), (wtf) removed before 6.14.
Hidden emoticons (oliver) and (soccer) debuted in Skype 5.9.
Group chats use P2P role system: Creator, Master, User, Applicant.
Only one Creator per chat; Masters cannot promote others to Master.
User role can post messages; Applicant waits for acceptance.
Commands /add, /kick, /setrole for group chat.
Commands /leave, /showmembers, /topic for group chat.
/alertsoff disables notifications; /me prefixes action-format message.
Online status: signed in, ready to receive calls/messages/files.
Away status: signed in but away; auto-switch after 5 minutes inactivity.
Do Not Disturb blocks pop-up notifications for calls/files/messages.
Invisible: user sees/interacts normally, appears Offline to others.
Offline: not signed in, cannot receive communications.
SkypeMe!: ready to receive calls from everybody; not available in all versions.
Country flags supported via (flag:XX) code format, e.g. (flag:US).
Group video calling for up to 10 people made free on Mac/Windows/Xbox One.
Dec 2013 Microsoft gave away free for 12 months features reserved for $9.99/month Premium.
Group video calling originally launched as premium service Jan 2011 at $4.99/day or $8.99/month.
Skype for Windows 8 supported free group calls/screen sharing for up to 10 people, previously premium-only.
With Skype 6.0, Messenger users signing in gained screen sharing, mobile video calling, Facebook video calling, group video calling.
Aug 2014 'active endpoints' smart notifications sent only to actively used device.
Active-endpoints rollout required most current Skype version, rolled out over several weeks from Aug 20, 2014.
As of March 2013, Skype created no native recording; third-party tools produced MP4 (video) and MP3 (audio) files.
Skype supported free conference calls/video/screen sharing up to 25 people, later expanded to 50 by ~April 2019.
